programme.title: Scotland's Finest: The Story of the Highland Games
programme.desc: Bill Patterson narrates the story of the Highland Games, recounting a tale of history, pageantry and characters that have shaped a Scottish phenomenon. From the battling clans through to Queen Victoria's infatuation with her Highland subjects, the Games have become a symbol of community and identity in Scotland and across the world.

programme.title: Genius of the Ancient World

programme.title: Lost Cities of The Ancients

programme.desc: In the Lambeyeque valley in northern Peru lies a strange lost world, the forgotten ruins of 250 mysterious pyramids, including some of the biggest on the planet, colossal structures made out of mud bricks.

programme.title: Inside Porton Down: Britain's Secret Weapons Research Facility
programme.desc: Dr Michael Mosley investigates Britain's most secretive and controversial military research base, Porton Down, on its 100th anniversary. He comes face-to-face with chemical and biological weapons old and new; reveals the truth about shocking animal and human testing and discovers how the latest science and technology are helping to defend us against terrorist attacks and rogue nations.

programme.title: The Ruth Ellis Files: A Very British Crime Story
programme.desc: In April 1955 Ruth Ellis shot her lover David Blakely dead. It's a case that shocked the nation and it still fascinates today. It has its place in ushering in the defence of diminished responsibility and the abolishment of capital punishment.

programme.title: Stephen Poliakoff Remembers... Caught on a Train

programme.title: Playhouse
programme.desc: A young Englishman, travelling on the Ostend to Vienna express, shares a train compartment with an American girl and an elderly Viennese lady.

programme.title: How to Get Ahead
programme.desc: Stephen Smith explores Renaissance Florence under the reign of Grand Duke Cosimo Medici. Cosimo's fledgling court prized the finer things in life and some of the greatest painters, sculptors and craftsmen in world history came to serve the Grand Duke. However, successful courtiers had to have brains as well as brawn. The canniest of them looked to theorists like Niccolò Machiavelli for underhand ways to get ahead, whilst enlightened polymaths turned their minds to the heavens, and to ice cream.

programme.title: Dambusters Declassified
programme.desc: Martin Shaw takes a fresh look at one of the most famous war stories of them all. The actor, himself a pilot, takes to the skies to retrace the route of the 1943 raid by 617 Squadron which used bouncing bombs to destroy German dams. He sheds new light on the story as he separates the fact from the myth behind this tale of courage and ingenuity.

programme.title: Whitney at the BBC
programme.desc: A reflection on Whitney Houston's best performances at the BBC celebrates the hit songs of one of the most successful artists in the world. Taking a sonic trip through the star's career, from the 1985 hit 'Saving all My Love for you', all the way through the 80s, 90s and 00s, this selection of songs educates on the artist's appeal to audiences everywhere and her ability to gain longstanding fans across multiple decades. It also reflects on why the singer's untimely death was such a deep loss.

programme.title: Whitney Houston: The Concert for a New South Africa (Durban)
programme.desc: In 1994, Whitney Houston took the stage in Durban, South Africa, making her the first major Western musician to visit the newly unified, post-apartheid nation following President Nelson Mandela's winning election. More than a concert, it was a celebration of freedom, hope, and unity. Whitney's powerhouse voice and emotional delivery brought joy and inspiration to a country newly liberated.

programme.title: WhatsApp Obsession: The Murder of Stephanie Hansen
programme.desc: On the 30th of December, 2022, 39-year-old Stephanie Hansen was brutally stabbed to death in her London home - her housemate and friend Sheldon Rodrigues initially appeared grief-stricken, yet behind his facade lay a chilling obsession. In the months before Stephanie's death, Rodrigues planted secret cameras and recording devices in their home and bombarded her with coercive WhatsApp messages - when Steph began a new relationship, his jealousy turned deadly. Through exclusive access to police bodycam footage, WhatsApp records and court evidence, this film reveals how the Metropolitan Police exposed Rodrigues' lies and uncovered the disturbing level of surveillance Steph was subjected to - featuring interviews with Steph's family, friends and the detectives who investigated the case, this powerful documentary unravels a story of obsession, control, and the ultimate betrayal.
